def: A short Markdown file at the root of a repository, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, loaded at the start of each session to tell a coding agent what it cannot work out from the code.
An open, plain-Markdown convention for a repository's instructions to coding agents, read by many tools and stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation.
A coding-agent mode in which the agent may read and search but not change anything, so exploration and planning cannot damage the repository.
A script that a coding tool runs automatically at a defined point, such as after an edit or before stopping, so an action happens every time regardless of what the model decides.
A cycle in which an agent edits, runs a check such as tests or a build, reads the result and iterates until the check passes, instead of stopping when its work looks done.
Using one session to implement a change and a separate fresh-context session to review it, so the reviewer is not anchored on the author's reasoning.
A second working directory of the same repository on its own branch, letting several agent sessions edit in parallel without overwriting each other.
The failure of accepting a plausible-looking implementation that has not been checked against edge cases or the real requirement.
The difference between how much faster people feel an AI tool makes them and the change in their measured task time, as seen in METR's 2025 trial.
A study that assigns each task at random to allow or disallow a tool, so that differences in time can be attributed to the tool rather than to who chose it.
